children: President Donald Trump is scheduled for a busy week, starting with the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where focus is expected to be on the Iran war, Ukraine and AI safety.
Trump will land in New York ​on Monday and will address the UN General Assembly Tuesday morning.

"The president will highlight how he has and his ​administration have confronted complex problems head-on around the world," said Mike Waltz, U.S. ambassador to the UN. "He will touch on the importance of ensuring that Iran never has a ​nuclear weapon… and he'll talk about some of the U.S.' accomplishments over the past year."

Trump will then meet with global leaders, including Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the UK's Andy Burnham, Japan's Sanae Takaichi and Venezuela's Delcy Rodriguez. He will also host a multilateral meeting with Arab leaders to discuss the Iran war.
Notably, China's President Xi Jinping will skip the UN General Assembly as he is scheduled for one-on-one talks with Trump in Washington on Thursday.
The UN General Assembly is being held at a time when the organization has struggled to maintain relevance.
"UN diplomacy aimed at halting wars and easing civilian suffering remains paralyzed, while funding cuts have weakened UN capacity," International Crisis Group, a think tank, observed last week.

Trump has slashed U.S. contributions to the organization and withdrawn from several UN bodies. "What is the purpose of the United Nations?" Trump questioned during his hourlong address at the General Assembly last year.
This year's session is also important as UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' term is ending and there's no clear frontrunner to replace him.

"The UN's fortunes over the next 12 months will depend in no small part on who its members select as the next Secretary-General," International Crisis Group stated. "She or he will face considerable pressure to hit the ground running and deliver quick wins for an organization whose credibility has waned."
